beat_player.text: {player} held the ridge longer than I expected. {troop_count} of yours still walked off it. Well fought, ser.
{player}, you left {gold} gold on that field. Keep it, I have coin enough and no appetite for it. Come back when your men have eaten.
{player}, you lost {troop_count} men to a hill you chose badly. I have held worse ground with fewer. Ride on, and mind the marsh path.
Ser {player}, a fine fight. You thought the ridge was yours and it nearly was. I would ride with you again if the road allowed it.
{player}, you pressed well today. Take {gold} gold for your trouble and tell your captains the ford is safer at dusk.

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat me fair. Lost {troop_count} to a better plan. I have lost more wars than most have logged hours. Still standing.
{player}, you took the field and I took the lesson. Send me a note if you want the reasons. I will not hide them.
Ser {player}, you have my respect. Lost {troop_count} men to your line. Next time we meet on ground I choose, mind.
{player}, that was luck on a wet field. I lost {troop_count} to it, and I will remember the spot.
{player}, the field is yours. Lost {troop_count} men and a morning. Tell me, did you choose that ridge or did it choose you?

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} held the flank while {enemy_faction} broke on the road. Good work, that was a proper afternoon.
{player}, you stood where you were needed against {enemy_faction}. Not many do that without being asked. Thank you.
We broke {enemy_faction} at the ford today. {player} kept the line steady. Fair work for an ordinary day.
{player}, you did your share against {enemy_faction}. I counted. Do not expect me to say it twice.

released_by_player.text: {player}, you let me walk when a ransom would have paid well. I will not forget that, and I do not forget debts.
{player} released me without asking for a ransom. Rare courtesy on this road. Give them a good word when you see them.
{player}, you could have held me for gold and you did not. Noted. I will settle it on the next field.
{player} let me go rather than sell me. Odd mercy from a hard face. I do not trust it, but I thank it.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome. Keep your boots dry and your word drier.
{player}, welcome to {my_faction}. Stay, and I will show you the bad roads first, before the good ones fool you.
{player} joined {my_faction} this morning. We will see how long they last on the marsh road. Patience first.
{player}, you have come under {my_faction}. I will watch your first march closely. A banner is not a shield.
New blood in {my_faction}. {player}, the old hands here will teach you what the first war taught us. Do not rush it.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been given {fief}. Hold it well. A town is easy to win and harder to keep, as I learned at the first war.
{player}, you have {fief} now. A town needs bread before banners. Keep it fed before you think of more.
{player}, the lord gave you {fief} and I wonder what it cost someone else. I will watch how you keep it.
So {fief} goes to {player}. Fine. Let us see if the walls hold longer than the last man who kept them.
{player}, {fief} is a fine place. I am glad it fell to someone who will not sell the granary. Congratulations, ser.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Our parties meet on a poor road. Water your horses and we can talk a while.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Your men look tired, and so do mine. Rest the column before we speak of anything else.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Step aside from the ford and we have nothing to say. Do not make me repeat it.
Well met, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, and I have seen worse roads than this one. Ride safe, the marsh is close.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I have held this road before without drawing steel. Say your piece and keep your hands off the reins.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe road, {player}. Mind the marsh edge after dusk, it has taken better riders than either of us.
That will do for today, {player}. Keep your column tight and your torches lit.
We are done, {player}. Keep riding, and do not come back to this ford unless you have a better argument.
Go well, {player}. Come find me at the old waystone if you want the story of the first war.
Farewell, {player}. Good talk, if a short one.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. The road to {village} will be mud until the thaw. Pack an extra cloak.
Lost half a wagon to the bog outside {village} last night. Keep to the stones, friends.
Someone asked me today if the old walls of {town} still stand. They do, and so do the men who built them.
The marsh fog is thick over the road to {village}. Keep your lanterns lit and your tempers low.
Late grain carts out of {town}. Mind your rations, the roads are long this season.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men in one bad morning. It happens to the best of us. Sit down, get some bread, and try again.
{player}, I saw the field go wrong. You lost {troop_count} and kept your head. That counts for more than the men.
{player} got caught on open ground and lost {troop_count} men. Nothing new on this road, but the lesson is still there.
{player}, {troop_count} men gone and no one to blame but the ground you chose. I will not gloat, but I noticed.
{player} lost {troop_count} on the flats. Grand plan, that. Nobody gets to be proud of that one, friend.
